question: Should OpenClaw add a core cross-gateway session messaging primitive for `sessions_send`/`sessions_spawn`, and what trust, scope, addressing, and delivery contract must it use before reviewing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/43656?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a narrow code defect: current source lacks the capability, the linked PR introduces new config and cross-gateway auth/message/session behavior, and repository policy treats this area as compatibility and security sensitive.

options.title: Approve a first-class federation contract
options.body: Specify the bridge identity, peer trust, operator scopes, addressing, delivery/idempotency, and upgrade-proof requirements, then update or replace the linked PR against that contract.

options.title: Keep it external for now
options.body: Document the supported MCP/plugin/relay workaround path and close or narrow core PRs until a missing core API is identified.

options.title: Land a narrow peer-gateway tool extension
options.body: Accept a smaller `gateway.peers` shape only after security review, real multi-gateway proof, and tests show local behavior and upgrades remain unchanged.

recommendation.title: Approve a first-class federation contract
recommendation.body: Specify the bridge identity, peer trust, operator scopes, addressing, delivery/idempotency, and upgrade-proof requirements, then update or replace the linked PR against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available session/gateway product-history signal and current checked-out history touches the central tool surface.
